highlightAliases.old: Environmental: extrinsic factors contribute to 35–45% of injurious falls; 1/4 to 1/2 of falls occur away from home; a stairs fall carries ~2x the injury risk of other falls (p636–637).
highlightAliases.new: Environmental: it has been estimated that extrinsic factors are involved in 35–45% of injurious falls; 1/4 to 1/2 of falls occur away from home; a stairs fall carries ~2x the injury risk of other falls (p636–637).

highlightAliases.old: TUG test: rise from chair, walk 3 meters, turn, return, sit; a 25-study systematic review found limited predictive value and no validated cut-point (p637).
highlightAliases.new: TUG test: rise from chair, walk 3 meters, turn, return, sit; a 25-study systematic review found limited predictive value in community-dwelling older adults and no cut-point for impaired performance could be recommended (p637).

highlightAliases.old: Vision: first-eye cataract surgery → 34% fewer falls; second-eye surgery similar (~32%) but not statistically significant; keep post-op spectacle power change < ±0.75 diopter (p639). Updating glasses to correct prescription: evidence less clear — one RCT found no significant reduction, and another (vision assessment + treatment) increased falls by ~50% (p639). Single-lens distance glasses for habitual multifocal wearers: 40% fewer falls in the outdoor-active subgroup (p639). Home-safety modification for severe uncorrectable low vision: 41% fewer falls (p639).
highlightAliases.new: Vision: first-eye cataract surgery → 34% fewer falls; second-eye surgery similar (~32%) but not statistically significant; one prospective cohort study associated cataract surgery with fewer falls provided post-op spectacle lens power updates were cautious (less than ±0.75 diopter change) (p639). Updating glasses to correct prescription: evidence less clear — one RCT found no significant reduction, and another (vision assessment + treatment) increased falls by ~50% (p639). Single-lens distance glasses for habitual multifocal wearers: 40% fewer falls in the outdoor-active subgroup (p639). Home-safety modification for severe uncorrectable low vision: 41% fewer falls (p639).

highlightAliases.old: Medications: withdrawing centrally-acting drugs did NOT significantly reduce falls in the most recent systematic review (5 trials, 1309 participants; RaR 0.98, 95% CI 0.63–1.51) — better to prevent uptake than deprescribe later (p639). Avoid prescribing benzodiazepines/z-drugs/other psychotropics for insomnia unless there is a clear pattern of addiction or inability to complete a withdrawal program; consider nonpharmacological approaches (p639). Vitamin D: no benefit in community-dwelling older adults (even if deficient); may reduce falls in RACF residents (p639).

highlightAliases.old: Two large General-Practice-based trials (fractures n = 5451; serious fall injuries n = 9803) found NO significant reduction in falls or fractures — raises questions about funding/implementing interventions; multifactorial interventions work better when provided directly than when relying on referral to routine service providers (p641).
highlightAliases.new: Two large primary-care trials found no significant reduction in their respective primary outcomes: fractures in PreFIT (9,803 participants) and serious fall injuries in STRIDE (5,451 participants). Direct delivery and uptake of the intervention may matter when implementing prevention through existing services (p641; PreFIT, STRIDE).
